public_rationale: Epoch AI's May 14, 2026 model estimates $38 billion in upfront capital costs for a hypothetical one-gigawatt AI data center, giving context for the multibillion-cost component but falling outside the January–March 2026 reference quarter [e1]. CoreWeave reports a consolidated GAAP net loss for that quarter, not individual facilities' profit histories [e2]. Neither source establishes that comparable facilities lose money for at least their first five or six service years, or documents a facility earning sustained profit before year five [e1, e2]. The model also supplies no realized revenue history from which to establish recovery of the initial investment [e1].
limitations: The hypothetical one-gigawatt model does not establish a general minimum upfront funding requirement [e1].
The packet lacks matched facility construction accounts, commissioning dates and multiyear profit histories [e1, e2].
The claim leaves the accounting basis for losses unspecified; periodic profit and cumulative recovery of upfront investment require separate measurements.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data centers cost billions upfront and, at best, run at a loss for their first five or six years, if they ever recover their costs.

statement.excerpt: AI data centers are ruinously expensive, requiring billions in upfront funding with operating costs so high that they, at best, run at a loss for the first five or six years of service, if they ever recover their original costs at all.

from_speaker: at best, run at a loss for the first five or six years of service
if they ever recover their original costs at all
our_interpretation: This is a general claim about facility economics, not a claim about one named operator's consolidated accounts.
The plain reading of run at a loss is negative periodic profit after relevant costs. It is distinct from taking several years to recover the initial investment.
At best is an asserted lower bound, not a conditional antecedent. A comparable facility achieving sustained profit before five years would challenge it.

I use the first quarter of 2026, the latest completed financial quarter before the post, as the reporting reference for the ongoing claim. Testing the duration also requires each facility's earlier operating history.
No accounting basis is identified. I do not silently substitute GAAP net income, adjusted EBITDA or a modeled capital-recovery period.
Ruinously expensive is evaluative; the checkable components are upfront funding and the asserted minimum loss duration.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable facility accounts establish multibillion upfront funding and losses throughout at least the first five years, with representative coverage sufficient to support the general claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable accounts for a comparable AI data center establish sustained profit before its fifth service anniversary, on the same identified accounting basis; representative cost records could also contradict the asserted general upfront funding requirement.

evidence.excerpt: Servers dominate this cost at $5 billion per year
evidence.explanation: The source models substantial capital-related costs for a hypothetical one-gigawatt facility. Annualizing equipment costs is not evidence of five or six years of actual losses, and the model is outside the target quarter.

evidence.locator: Forward-Looking Statements, final sentence; financial tables elsewhere on the page
evidence.explanation: The release reports a consolidated GAAP net loss and separately presents non-GAAP measures. It provides neither facility-level profit histories nor evidence of a universal minimum loss duration.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable facility-level construction costs, commissioning dates and periodic accounts on an explicit accounting basis. Representative histories showing losses throughout the first five or six years would support the duration claim; sustained profit at a comparable facility before its fifth anniversary would contradict the asserted minimum. Cumulative cash-flow records would separately address capital recovery.
